validated_work_order.understanding: All three follow-ups from #44 reproduce on main as filed, and all three are kept. (1) Review: the fixture guard in the #44 test (test/web/pages.test.js, the 'seeded' assertion before the render loop) counts only lead_qualified events — the denominator. The spend.observed row that carries 3_000_000_000 micros is the numerator and is unguarded, so a fixture that stops carrying the amount still passes the guard and then fails at the CPL assertion with 'got —', which reads as a currency regression. Verified: the guard filters on event_type === 'lead_qualified' and asserts a count of 1. (2) Review: the same test re-creates the tenant_usd + opp_usd_expensive block (4 occurrences of the id, in 2 identical create blocks at lines 930-940 and 977-987) and the seven-line `envelope` closure that already exists twice more in the file (lines 295, 339, 1001 — three copies, differing only in the tenant_id literal). freshRepos()/seededRepos() at lines 24 and 30 are the file's established idiom for this. The reviewer's own note says the fence around the two existing USD tests belongs to whoever owns the order — that is this order, and it is lifted here deliberately. (3) QA: ISO_CURRENCIES.includes is exact, so a tenant row holding 'usd', 'Usd' or ' USD ' never resolves. I reproduced this against main and it is WORSE than the report says, so the 'minor' severity does not stand. For a 'usd' tenant the opportunity row renders 'value ₹6,000.00' as reported, and the dashboard draws all six Meta amounts in rupees (₹500.00, ₹1,000.00, ₹250.00 in the ad-set table; ₹4,000.00, ₹8,750.00, ₹1,250.00 in the insights table). The Qualified CPL tile also reads '—', and GET /v1/metrics reports spend_micros 0, and POST /v1/events 400s CURRENCY_MISMATCH on a legitimate USD spend for such a tenant. The blast radius is still narrow and the trigger is external: normaliseGrowthEvent validates ingest currency against ISO_CURRENCIES exactly, and routes.js seeds a new tenant's currency from that validated code, so nothing the app itself writes today produces a non-canonical code. The bug is that the read path is not defensive about a row it did not write (a human UPDATE, a legacy import, a future write path). CORRECTION carried into this version: the em-dash on the SHIPPED SEED is not the defect, and this order does not claim it is. The seed's only spend row (evt_seed_journey_spend_1) carries currency 'INR' (scripts/seed.js:24). So a 'usd' tenant whose spend rows are all INR correctly sums to nothing and correctly renders the em-dash — that is computeFunnel's foreign-currency exclusion working, not a canonicalisation failure. What the defect removes is the case where the tenant's own unit of account and its own spend agree, the spend is simply labelled 'USD' or 'usd' differently from the row: there the exclusion drops the tenant's real spend, the CPL goes null, and the ingest path 400s a legitimate event. The v1 plan conflated the two and would have sent QA to fail AC-2 on a correct build.
validated_work_order.root_cause: One exact-match membership test standing in for currency identity, at every point where a STORED TENANT code is read. A tenant code is stored as an arbitrary string (tenants.create takes any string; the column is TEXT), but three consumers compare it by exact string equality: money()'s ISO_CURRENCIES.includes guard in src/web/pages.js:222, computeFunnel's tenant-currency exclusion as fed from src/web/pages.js:377 and src/api/routes.js:170, and the CURRENCY_MISMATCH check at src/api/routes.js:146. 'usd' and 'USD' name the same unit of account, so all three treat the tenant's own spend as foreign and either relabel it or drop it. Nothing canonicalises between the row and those comparisons. The asymmetry that makes the fix safe: the tenant row is the only untrusted side of every one of these comparisons. The other side — an event's payload currency — is already canonical, because normaliseGrowthEvent rejects anything outside ISO_CURRENCIES exactly (src/domain/measurement.js:120, :134) before the row is ever compared to it. So canonicalise the stored row, never the event payload, and never inside computeFunnel.
validated_work_order.approach: Add one exported boundary function to the domain — canonicalCurrency(code) in src/domain/money.js, which trims and upper-cases a stored string and returns the ISO 4217 code it names, or null when it names none ('ZZZ' still resolves to null, so the documented bad-data INR fallback and the never-500 behaviour are unchanged). Then resolve every read of a tenant row's currency through it, in one seam per module, rather than touching the comparisons individually: pages.js gets a local tenantCurrency(tenant) helper used at all EIGHT `tenant?.currency ?? 'INR'` / `tenant.currency ?? 'INR'` read sites (v1 said six and then enumerated eight; the measured list is below), and money() itself canonicalises before the fallback so any value that reaches the renderer by another path still draws its own unit. routes.js gets a local helper used at both reads of the row — the metrics funnel filter and the CURRENCY_MISMATCH check — with the comparison canonicalising while the 400's message and details keep reporting the stored string verbatim, so every existing 400 is byte-identical and only the mis-cased tenant changes from rejected to accepted. computeFunnel is NOT changed: it keeps its exact string comparison and is simply fed a canonical code, because its event-payload side is already guaranteed canonical by ingest. That is also what keeps the QA BUG-2 foreign-currency exclusion intact — a 'usd' tenant must still exclude a genuinely INR spend row, and a new test now pins that so a future implementer cannot 'fix' the em-dash by summing foreign spend. Read-side only, deliberately: the QA repro sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE, which never touches tenants.create, so a write-side fix would not have fixed the reported case; and the existing test at test/web/pages.test.js:1077 pins tenants.create accepting any string, so tightening the write path would break a deliberate contract for no gain on the reported defect. Separately, close the two review findings in the same test file: lift the repeated tenant+opportunity block into a usdRepos() helper beside freshRepos() and the repeated envelope closure into one tenant-parameterised validatedEnvelope(), and have all three call sites use them; and extend the fixture guard to assert the resolved spend amount alongside the qualified-lead count, so a broken numerator fails at the guard with a fixture-shaped message instead of surfacing at the money assertion as an em-dash.

files.change: Export a new canonicalCurrency(currency): trims and upper-cases a stored code and returns the ISO 4217 code it names, or null when it names none (non-string, empty/whitespace, or an unknown code like 'ZZZ'). Implementation: `if (typeof currency !== 'string') return null; const code = currency.trim().toUpperCase(); return ISO_CURRENCIES.includes(code) ? code : null;`. Document why case and whitespace are not currency errors and why a genuinely unknown code is still a data error. Leave assertValidCurrency strict: fromMicros/toMicros' contract stays 'a code I can render', and loosening it would change INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour test/domain/money.test.js already pins. The new function is the read-time boundary for a STORED row, not a second constructor and not a normaliser for event payloads (those are validated exactly at ingest already).
files.why: One place decides what a stored code means. TR-1: a tenant's amounts carry a real ISO unit of account.

acceptance.check: After a USD spend.observed of 3_000_000_000 micros is accepted for the 'usd' tenant, the Qualified CPL tile on / reads '$1,000.00' and must not read '—'. The arithmetic, which is the whole content of this criterion: the tenant's own USD spend is 3_000_000_000 micros (the seeded INR spend row of 7_200_000_000 stays excluded — that exclusion is correct and must NOT change), qualified_volume is 3 (the three seeded lead_qualified rows; the step appends no lead), so 3_000_000_000 / 3 = 1_000_000_000 micros = $1,000.00. The invariant is spend_micros / qualified_volume, so this figure holds only for a step that appends exactly one USD spend and no lead; appending a lead as well would make it $750.00, and that is a different criterion, not this one. What the defect removes is that on main the POST that creates this situation is itself a 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH, so the tile cannot be given a number at all. Note for the reader: the '$3,000.00' in test/web/pages.test.js is a DIFFERENT fixture (a fresh database, one qualified lead, no seed rows) and deliberately does not match this one.

qa_script: Set the environment up ONCE, so the seed and the server provably share one database file: `export PORT=3100` then `export DB_PATH=$(mktemp -d)/qa58.db`, then `npm run sdlc:seed`, then `npm run sdlc:serve &`, then retry `npm run sdlc:ready` until it returns 200 (it probes http://localhost:$PORT/health and $PORT is exported, so it targets 3100). Confirm the seed and the serve agree before going further: `sqlite3 $DB_PATH 'SELECT id,currency FROM tenants;'` must print exactly one row, `tenant_demo|INR`. Every later UPDATE below is written as `sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE ...; SELECT changes();"` and MUST print 1 — a 0 means the wrong DB_PATH, and the run is void rather than passed.

The regression this ticket exists to remove, on the shipped app, with the seeded database still at INR. Measured on main, unmodified: /opportunities first row reads 'value ₹6,000.00'; / draws six rupee amounts in its Meta tables (₹500.00, ₹1,000.00, ₹250.00, ₹4,000.00, ₹8,750.00, ₹1,250.00); the Qualified CPL tile reads '—'; GET /v1/metrics reports spend_micros 0 with qualified_cpl_micros null; and POST of a USD spend.observed to tenant_demo is a 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH with details {tenant_currency:'INR', received:'USD'}. After this change, /, /opportunities and /experiments must contain no '₹' at all for that tenant, and the POST must be a 202.

`sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE tenants SET currency = 'usd' WHERE id = 'tenant_demo'; SELECT changes();"` — must print 1. Reload /opportunities: the first [data-testid=opportunity-row] (data-opportunity-id='opp_seed_expensive') must read 'value $6,000.00' and 'cost $1,900.00'. Reload /: [data-testid=meta-adSets] must contain '$500.00' and [data-testid=meta-insights] must contain '$4,000.00'. Reload /experiments: the caps line must read 'Max spend $500.00 · max downside $200.00'. Then assert the strong form: grep each of the three response bodies for the rupee sign and require zero hits — measured on main this tenant draws 6, 6 and 4 of them, so 'no ₹500.00 and no ₹4,000.00' would pass on a build that still mislabels five other amounts.

`curl -s -X POST localhost:$PORT/v1/events -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"event_id":"evt_qa_usd_spend_1","event_name":"spend.observed","occurred_at":"2026-09-25T08:00:00.000Z","currency":"USD","value":3000000000,"campaign":"qa-usd","session_id":"sess_qa_1"}'` — must be 202 with {"receipt":"evt_qa_usd_spend_1","appended":true,"duplicate":false} (it is a 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH on main; the body above is known-good, proven by posting it to a fresh tenant id, which auto-creates as USD and returns exactly this 202). Reload / and read the kpi-value inside the Qualified CPL kpi-card: it must be '$1,000.00', not '—'. Arithmetic: the tenant's own USD spend is 3_000_000_000 micros (the seeded 7_200_000_000 INR row stays excluded, correctly), over 3 qualified leads = 1_000_000_000 micros = $1,000.00. Then set the currency to ' USD ' and to 'Usd' in turn, re-running the two page reads each time, and require identical money strings.

API agreement: `curl -s "localhost:$PORT/v1/metrics?tenant_id=tenant_demo" | jq '{spend_micros, qualified_volume, qualified_cpl_micros}'` must report spend_micros 3000000000, qualified_volume 3, qualified_cpl_micros 1000000000 — the same $1,000.00 the page shows, not zero and not null.

Control, unchanged bad-data behaviour: `sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE tenants SET currency = 'ZZZ' WHERE id = 'tenant_demo'; SELECT changes();"` — must print 1. /opportunities must still return HTTP 200 and its first row must still read 'value ₹6,000.00' (the INR fallback; opp_seed_expensive ranks first at score 0.9208), the response must not contain the string 'ZZZ', and POSTing the same USD spend.observed must still be 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH with message 'tenant tenant_demo keeps ZZZ; spend in USD was rejected' and details {tenant_currency:'ZZZ', received:'USD'}. This control is the one that proves the INR fallback was not weakened: a 'ZZZ' row must NOT be treated as USD by the new code.

Control, genuine mismatch in the other direction: set the currency back to 'USD' (assert changes() = 1) and POST a spend.observed with currency EUR — still 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH, details {tenant_currency:'USD', received:'EUR'}.

Also confirm the em-dash is still reachable for a genuinely foreign spend, so AC-2's number has not been reached by summing foreign currency: with the currency back at 'usd' and the posted USD spend removed from consideration by setting the currency to 'INR' instead, reload / — the Qualified CPL tile must read '—', because every remaining spend row is INR-denominated and the INR seed row is then the only one in the tenant's own unit. `npm run sdlc:verify` green, and the two greps in AC-5 at their required counts.
evidence: Every number in this work order was measured on this checkout, not read off the report. Seeded a temp database, set tenants.currency = 'usd', posted a USD spend.observed of 3_000_000_000 through the repository, and ran computeFunnel over the live rows: computeFunnel(rows, 'usd') — today's code path — returns {spend_micros: 0, qualified_volume: 3, qualified_cpl_micros: null}, and computeFunnel(rows, 'USD') — the post-fix canonical code — returns {spend_micros: 3000000000, qualified_volume: 3, qualified_cpl_micros: 1000000000}, which is $1,000.00.

The seeded database already holds three lead_qualified rows (evt_seed_journey_lead_qualified_1..3, scripts/seed.js:41-55), so any step that appends a fourth lead changes the denominator and the expected CPL to $750.00. The criterion therefore appends no lead.

The seed's only spend row is evt_seed_journey_spend_1 with payload {campaign:'search-brand', amount_micros: 7_200_000_000, currency: 'INR'} (scripts/seed.js:21-25). This is the review's objection 1, confirmed at source: on a 'usd' tenant that row is correctly excluded, so the em-dash on the bare seed is correct behaviour and is NOT what this change removes.

Review option (a) for objecting to it — rewriting the spend row's currency with `UPDATE raw_events SET payload = json_set(...)` — is not available in this application at all. raw_events carries the trigger raw_events_append_only_update (src/data/db.js, migration 002), and running that exact statement through the sqlite3 CLI fails with 'raw_events is append-only: UPDATE denied' (exit 19). Verified in the same environment the QA script runs in. Option (b), posting the spend through ingest, is the only route, and it is the route that also exercises the CURRENCY_MISMATCH fix, so it covers AC-2 and AC-3 with one action.

Rendering /opportunities, / and /experiments on the seeded database with tenant_demo = 'usd', unmodified main, with the Meta provider wired as the route wires it: the opportunity page's first row reads 'value ₹6,000.00' and the page carries six rupee amounts (₹6,000.00, ₹1,900.00, ₹2,000.00, ₹100.00, ₹1,000.00, ₹500.00); / carries six (₹500.00, ₹1,000.00, ₹250.00 from the ad-set table and ₹4,000.00, ₹8,750.00, ₹1,250.00 from insights); /experiments carries four (₹500.00, ₹200.00, ₹300.00, ₹100.00). The rupee counts are the reason AC-1 asserts the absence of the character and not the absence of two named amounts.

The / route only draws its Meta tables when a metaProvider is passed, which buildApp does and a bare renderPage call does not. A QA or unit check that calls renderPage('/') without a provider sees no Meta amounts at all and cannot verify AC-1's dashboard half — this is why the test case names the provider explicitly.

API shapes on main, measured through buildApp: a 'usd' tenant posting a USD spend.observed is 400 {code:'CURRENCY_MISMATCH', message:'tenant tenant_demo keeps usd; spend in USD was rejected', details:{tenant_currency:'usd', received:'USD'}}; a 'ZZZ' tenant is 400 with the same shape and tenant_currency 'ZZZ'; a 'USD' tenant posting EUR is 400 with details {tenant_currency:'USD', received:'EUR'}; and GET /v1/metrics reports spend_micros 0, qualified_volume 3, qualified_cpl_micros null for all three. The two controls' message and details strings are quoted verbatim in AC-3 because the fix must leave them byte-identical.

The exact POST body in qa_script step 4 is known-good: posted to a fresh tenant id, which auto-creates with the validated event currency USD, it returns 202 {"receipt":"evt_qa_usd_spend_1","appended":true,"duplicate":false}. So a 400 on tenant_demo after this change is the currency bug, not a malformed request.

The `SELECT changes()` guard works against this database: `sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE tenants SET currency='usd' WHERE id='tenant_demo'; SELECT changes();"` prints 1, and a following `SELECT id,currency FROM tenants;` prints `tenant_demo|usd`. The sqlite3 CLI is present at /usr/bin/sqlite3 (3.45.1), so the QA script does not depend on it being absent.

The eight tenant-currency read sites in src/web/pages.js are at lines 326, 346, 377, 390, 744, 758, 833 and 849, and money()'s ISO_CURRENCIES guard is at line 222 with the import at line 12. The v1 plan said 'all six' and then enumerated eight; the eight are what this order names.

Fixture duplication counts on main: 'opp_usd_expensive' occurs 4 times in test/web/pages.test.js, in two identical create blocks at lines 930-940 and 977-987; 'const envelope = (event_id' occurs 3 times, at lines 295, 339 and 1001. The #44 test's guard, at the point before the render loop, filters on event_type === 'lead_qualified' and asserts a count of 1, and no assertion before the render loop touches the spend.observed amount — review finding 1 confirmed.
Suite size on main, for AC-6: 275 tests pass with 0 failures across the whole run, of which 51 are in test/web/pages.test.js. (The v1 order said 49; that figure was stale.)
risks: money() is the last line before a number reaches a reader, so its fallback now depends on canonicalCurrency. A code that resolves to a real ISO currency but whose MINOR_EXPONENTS entry is missing (a 0- or 3-digit currency such as JPY or BHD) now renders where it previously fell back to INR. That is the correct unit, and microsPerMinorUnit already defaults to 2 for those, so the split maths is unchanged — but it is a real behaviour change for any tenant whose code is a valid non-2-exponent currency written in lower case, and it is the intended fix.

Relaxing the ingest mismatch check means a 'usd' tenant now accepts USD spend it used to reject. That is the point, but it is the one place where this order makes the write path more permissive, so the genuine-mismatch controls in the tests, in AC-3 and in qa_script steps 6 and 7 matter: 'USD' tenant + EUR spend, and 'ZZZ' tenant + USD spend, must both still 400 with the stored string reported verbatim.

The temptation this ticket creates is the one the review already caught once: reading the em-dash on the bare seed as the bug and 'fixing' it by making computeFunnel sum foreign-currency spend. That would break QA BUG-2, which is the reason the exclusion exists. The fix is to canonicalise the stored tenant row, never the event payload and never the comparison inside computeFunnel, and tests[] pins the negative case ('a usd tenant whose only spend row is denominated in another currency still reads the em-dash') so the temptation fails the suite instead of shipping.

The CURRENCY_MISMATCH error's message and details keep the stored string verbatim, so an operator with a 'usd' row who now gets a 202 sees no message at all; the canonicalisation is silent by design. Accepted: the row is bad data, the numbers are right, and no in-app write path produces the row.

The test-file refactor touches two existing USD tests that the #44 work order fenced off. The fence is lifted by this order, deliberately, at the reviewer's own suggestion, so a reviewer who does not know that will read the diff as a constraint violation. The change must be a pure move: no assertion in either test may change, and AC-5's two greps are the mechanical check.

usdRepos() returning a repos object with tenant and opportunity pre-seeded means a caller that also needs events or an experiment mutates it further. If an implementer instead threads options through the helper, the call sites stop being one-liners and the indirection cost returns.
out_of_scope: Rejecting a non-canonical code on write (tenants.create throwing or coercing). The issue offers it as the alternative, and it is the weaker of the two here: the QA repro sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE, which never reaches tenants.create, so a write-side guard would not fix the reported case and would break the deliberate 'accepts any string, render must not 500' contract pinned at test/web/pages.test.js:1077.

Repairing existing non-canonical tenant rows in storage — a migration or a seed-time normalisation. Nothing in the app writes such rows today (see evidence), the read-side fix makes them render correctly wherever they exist, and a data migration on a table a human can edit is a separate decision with its own rollback story.

Changing the seed's spend row to be USD-denominated, so that the bare seeded database would show a dollar CPL for a 'usd' tenant. It would have made the v1 acceptance criterion true, but the INR seed spend is what makes the INR default tenant correct and the exclusion observable, and rewriting shipped demo data to suit a test is the wrong direction. The QA fixture supplies its own USD spend instead, over HTTP, through the path the ticket is actually about.

Making computeFunnel canonicalise the event payload currency, or comparing currencies there with anything other than exact equality. Ingest guarantees payload currencies are already canonical (normaliseGrowthEvent rejects anything outside ISO_CURRENCIES), so there is nothing to normalise on that side, and loosening the comparison would re-open the QA BUG-2 hole the exclusion closed.
The Meta error-shell test at test/web/pages.test.js:1059, which needs a tenant and no opportunity. It keeps its own single-line tenants.create; do not widen usdRepos() to serve it.
The two mixed-currency tenant_demo tests' fixtures beyond their envelope closures. They share validatedEnvelope() and nothing else.

Any change to assertValidCurrency, fromMicros, toMicros or the INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour in src/domain/money.js. canonicalCurrency is a read-time boundary, not a second constructor, and loosening the constructor is a separate decision about the money contract.

/journal and /approvals. Neither draws an amount — the only money renderers in src/web/pages.js are money(), reached from the Meta tables, the KPI strip, the opportunity rows and the experiment cards — so they cannot exhibit this defect and AC-1 does not name them.

Splitting the ticket. Findings 1 and 2 are the same file and the same test, and finding 3 is the defect that test guards; the reviewer explicitly asked for the fixture lift to be owned by whoever writes the order. Planning them together is cheaper than three trips through the council, and the ticket says to split only if they turn out to be unrelated.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim and every number in this order was executed against this checkout rather than read off the report, and the review's three objections were each reproduced before being answered: the seed's INR spend row, the four-lead denominator, and the two-temp-directory command. The design was not re-litigated — the objections were all about the work order's fixture arithmetic, not the canonicalisation choice — so the change is still one function plus eight mechanical read-site replacements and one comparison, with no new dependency, no schema change and no forbidden path. The 11 points held back are the DRY refactor: it touches two tests this ticket's own predecessor fenced off, it is a pure move across roughly 90 lines, and it is the kind of change that can quietly alter a fixture. AC-5 makes it mechanically checkable, and the implementer must run test/web/pages.test.js before and after, not just after.

alternatives_considered.approach: Canonicalise in tenants.create on write, coercing the stored row to its canonical form.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not fix the reported repro, which sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE and never reaches the repository. It would also break the contract test/web/pages.test.js:1077 pins — that tenants.create accepts any string and a page render must not 500 on bad data — and it would silently rewrite operator-supplied data. Read-side canonicalisation covers every source of a bad row, which is a superset of what write-side covers.

alternatives_considered.approach: Reject the non-canonical code at the render boundary: keep the INR fallback but return an error panel or an unformatted 'USD 6,000.00' when the stored code is merely mis-cased.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The money() doc comment already argues the opposite trade deliberately — a correctly-formatted amount in the repo default over a mislabelled-but-honest one. And the honest-label option does not help here: 'usd' is not bad data in the way 'ZZZ' is, it is the same currency with different typing, and a reader seeing 'USD 6,000.00' instead of '$6,000.00' learns nothing was wrong.

alternatives_considered.approach: Loosen assertValidCurrency in money.js so fromMicros itself accepts and normalises 'usd', and let the three comparison sites stay as they are.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes the money constructor's contract rather than its consumers, so the INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour test/domain/money.test.js already pins moves for every caller, and it still does not fix computeFunnel's tenant-currency comparison, which is a string compare with no money constructor in it. The defect is at the read boundary, so that is where the fix belongs.

alternatives_considered.approach: Verify the CPL fix by rewriting the seeded spend row's currency in place, as the review's objection 1 option (a) suggests: UPDATE raw_events SET payload = json_set(payload,'$.currency','USD').
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is not available: raw_events carries the raw_events_append_only_update trigger, and the exact statement fails in the sqlite3 CLI with 'raw_events is append-only: UPDATE denied' (exit 19), verified in this environment. The seeded data is append-only by design (TR-20), so the QA fixture has to arrive through ingest, which is the path the ticket is about anyway.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make AC-2 a weaker claim — assert only that the CPL tile is not the em-dash, without naming the number.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That is the same comment-promises-more-than-it-delivers shape the review finding this ticket exists to remove, one layer up. It is also strictly weaker than available: the QA fixture is fully determined, so the number can be computed and stated, and a criterion that can be computed and stated should be. The number is $1,000.00, with the arithmetic in AC-2.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the currency defect in this ticket and file findings 1 and 2 as a separate cleanup issue.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The ticket bundles them on purpose and the reviewer's own note on finding 2 asks for the fixture lift to be owned by whoever holds the order. All three land in test/web/pages.test.js plus the currency path that file guards, and the new canonicalisation test wants the very helper findings 1 and 2 ask for. Splitting would mean the helper lands in one PR and the test that uses it in another.

assumptions: Trim-and-upper is the right canonicalisation for ISO 4217 codes, and no tenant needs a code that is legitimately mixed-case or padded. ISO 4217 codes are upper-case alpha-3 by definition, so the mapping is total on well-formed input and a no-op on canonical input.

A mis-cased or padded tenant code is bad data, not a distinct unit of account, and no tenant row anywhere in the wild holds a code that canonicalises to something other than what was meant. The only sources are a human UPDATE and a legacy import; the app's own write path already emits canonical codes.

The stored tenant row is the only side of every currency comparison that needs canonicalising. The event-payload side is validated exactly at ingest (normaliseGrowthEvent rejects anything outside ISO_CURRENCIES before the comparison is reached), so there is no second untrusted spelling to handle.
unknowns: Whether any deployed database outside this repo holds a non-canonical tenant row. Nothing in the repo enumerates tenants beyond the demo one, and the read-side fix makes such a row render correctly whether or not it exists, so the answer does not change the work — it changes only whether QA ever sees the bug in the wild.

Whether a tenant row could ever legitimately hold a currency outside ISO_CURRENCIES that this build should still render. The 'ZZZ' test says no: unknown is bad data and INR is the documented fallback. This ticket does not revisit that decision, and qa_script step 6 keeps that control live.
residual_risks: A stored code that is mis-cased AND a currency with no 2-digit minor unit now renders in its own unit for the first time, where before it drew rupees. If any such row exists, the numbers a reader sees will change currency on upgrade. That is the fix, not a regression, and no test asserts the old value for such a row — but QA should read the first AC-1 render as a deliberate change rather than a diff to be accepted at a glance.

A non-canonical row stays non-canonical in storage after this change. It renders correctly everywhere now, but the next reader of the tenants table sees 'usd' and may reasonably assume the app normalises on write. It does not. The fix is stated at the read boundary in the money() doc comment, which is the only place a future implementer is likely to be looking.

Because raw_events is append-only, an operator who realises a tenant row is mis-cased cannot repair the affected spend rows once they have been written in the wrong unit — the events stay foreign and stay excluded, and the CPL stays null. The read-side fix makes such a row render its own currency for everything else, so the remaining wrongness is confined to the funnel, and correcting it means new events rather than an edit. This is a property of the existing append-only design, not something this change introduces, and it is a reason the silent canonicalisation is acceptable rather than a reason to widen the ticket.
